title: Historic places to explore in Fort Kochi
description: Five landmarks that introduce the history of Fort Kochi.
intro: Fort Kochi’s historic places are close enough to shape a walking itinerary, but they serve different purposes: some are places of worship, some are museums and others are open-air landmarks. Confirm access arrangements and be considerate of worship and local activity.

entries.name: St Francis Church
entries.description: Kerala Tourism traces the church’s history to the early sixteenth century and records its Portuguese, Dutch and later Anglican connections. Vasco da Gama was initially buried here before his remains were taken to Portugal.

entries.name: Santa Cruz Cathedral Basilica
entries.description: The church’s foundation dates to 1505, while the present structure was consecrated in 1905. Kerala Tourism highlights its spires, Gothic-style interior and paintings; check current visiting arrangements around services.

entries.name: Chinese fishing nets
entries.description: These cantilevered fishing structures are one of the recognizable sights along the Fort Kochi shore. Vasco da Gama Square is a place identified by Kerala Tourism for observing the nets; use care around active fishing work.
entries.details: Working waterfront · Vasco da Gama Square

entries.name: Indo-Portuguese Museum
entries.description: Inside the Bishop’s House compound, the museum brings together objects from churches in the region. Its five collection themes provide context for the Portuguese influence on local art and religious life.

entries.name: Dutch Cemetery
entries.description: Kerala Tourism identifies the cemetery among Fort Kochi’s historical sites. Viewing and entry arrangements may vary, so check locally rather than assuming the grounds are open for visits.
